fields.title: Every corpus publishes, installs and is read back
fields.evidence: The `corpora`, `round-trip` and `import-round-trip` job logs on the pull request.

sections.What it checks:
* `eng:std-GATES.BUILD` says a push "**MUST** trigger a build and the test
  suite, without anyone asking for it".
* `std-PLUGIN.TYPES` says a skill "**MUST** name the parts file of the
  type its component declares, and no other type's".
* `std-PLUGIN.DECLARE` says every skill directory and hook directory
  in the plugin tree "**MUST** appear under `metadata.components`".
sections.How it works:
Three jobs share the work. `corpora` runs `export` and `pack` in each of the four corpora. `round-trip` runs `export` and `bundle` in each, on Ubuntu, and in `payments` on Windows too. `bundle` fails on a directory under `skills/` or `hooks/` that no component in `metadata.components` claims. Then `claude plugin validate --strict` runs over the assembled plugin and over its marketplace. `tooling/tests/bundled-components.sh` follows it. It fails a component `bundle.json` kept that is missing from the tree, or one it trimmed that is present. A component is a skill or hook directory, or a view's file. It also fails where `.claude-plugin/` contains anything but `plugin.json`.

In every cell but `dog-fooding`, `round-trip` then installs the plugin. It runs `bundled-components.sh` over the installed copy, then asks each skill in it the questions that skill describes. Where the build index ships, it checks that the build-index hook pushes at most 10,000 characters, and runs the installed script twice for one session to check that it prints once. It logs how long a later call takes on a small input and on a 200 KB one, and fails on neither.

`import-round-trip` publishes from `engineering`, consumes it from `payments`, renames a clause upstream, and asserts the downstream build fails and reports that clause.

The `tool` job adds the empty case. It bundles a corpus that adopted no type, then runs `claude plugin validate --strict` over the plugin and its marketplace. It asserts that nothing reading a type shipped, and that `raise-finding`, the one standalone skill, survived. No job installs that plugin.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
`round-trip` checks the `dog-fooding` plugin and installs none, because it is the same shape as `payments`. On Windows it runs `payments` alone, which takes the shell, the paths and the import path together.

`round-trip` reads one sentence of each skill. It greps `SKILL.md` for the parts file the component requires, and fails a skill that names another type's. Nothing else `std-PLUGIN` asks of the wording is checked here. Two of its rules are checked by [ctl-0009](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/de9670add3635664cbd011e5e78b8a9067de0474/examples/dog-fooding/controls/0009-tool-test-layers.md) instead, which is where the unit tests that read a skill's prose run.

`harvest-findings` travels into a corpus's working tree rather than into a plugin, so no job here reaches it. Every check above reads an assembled bundle, and that skill is in none. The clause saying no plugin may declare a component that triages findings has no control either.

Nothing here runs the publishing workflows. CI proves that a package and a plugin assemble. Whether nuget.org, GitHub Packages or the `marketplace` branch accepts either is answered after the merge.

The Claude Code CLI installs at `latest` in every one of these jobs, so a release of it can fail the gate with no change here.
